in_hebrew.name: היינריך
in_hebrew.long_meaning: היינריך הוא שם גרמני שמורכב מהמילים 'היין' שפירושו 'בית' ו'ריך' שפירושו 'שולט' או 'מלך'. השם נגזר מהשפה הגרמנית ומשמעותו 'שולט בבית' או 'מלך הבית'. אין לו קשר ישיר לשפה העברית או למקורותיה המקראיים.

in_greek.name: Χάινριχ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χάινριχ είναι γερμανικής προέλευσης και προέρχεται από τις λέξεις 'Χάιν' που σημαίνει 'σπίτι' και 'Ρίχ' που σημαίνει 'κυρίαρχος' ή 'βασιλιάς'. Το όνομα σημαίνει 'ο κυρίαρχος του οίκου' ή 'ο βασιλιάς του σπιτιού'. Δεν υπάρχει άμεση σύνδεση με την ελληνική γλώσσα ή τις βιβλικές ρίζες.

in_latin.name: Henricus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Henricus origine germanica est et componitur ex vocibus 'Hein' quae domum significat et 'Ric' quae dominum vel regem significat. Nomen igitur significat 'dominus domus' vel 'rex domus'. In ecclesia christiana primitiva, nomen Henricus habuit significationem nobilitas et potestatis.

in_english.name: Heinrich
in_english.meaning: Ruler of the Home or Estate
in_english.long_meaning: The name Heinrich is of Germanic origin, derived from the Old High German words 'hein' meaning 'home' or 'estate' and 'rich' meaning 'ruler' or 'king'. It signifies 'ruler of the home' or 'estate ruler'. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the name reflects a sense of leadership and stewardship, which are biblical values. Historically, the name has been popular among European royalty and nobility, emphasizing power and dominion. In Christian tradition, the name Heinrich conveys a sense of responsibility and authority.

saint_reference.note: Several saints and monarchs have borne the name Henry, reflecting its historical and spiritual significance in Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: The name Heinrich carries a significant weight in German and European cultural history. Throughout the Middle Ages, many prominent rulers, kings, and emperors bore this name. Heinrich I, the founder of the German kingdom in 936 AD, is one of the most notable figures. The name Heinrich is strongly associated with leadership and power, reflecting the values of medieval society.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Heinrich not only signifies temporal power and rule but also has spiritual significance. The Germanic elements haim (home) and ric (ruler, power) suggest that the name Heinrich refers to a spiritual ruler or guardian of a domestic sphere or a household. In a religious context, the name can be seen as a reminder of God as the ultimate ruler and provider of home or family. Thus, Heinrich resonates with both the material and spiritual aspects of human life.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Heinrich der Vogler (Heinrich the Fowler, 912-936 AD) was a German king of the Saxon dynasty. The name Heinrich carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Heinrich was the first king of Germany to be crowned with the Imperial Crown. He was also the first king to be called 'Reichs-König' (Emperor).

modern_usage.modern_context: Heinrich is a common name in the German-speaking world and is derived from the Old High German word 'heinric' meaning 'ruler of the home'. It was popularized by the historical figure Heinrich der Vogler.

name_in_real_life.story: Elizabeth Heinrich, a minister in Rome, Italy, shares that their name Heinrich meaning "Home ruler, owner of the house" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
